They do not apply themselves to that. They do not apply themselves to the idea that form "exists" or "does not exist." Likewise, they do not apply themselves to the idea that feelings, perceptions, mental formations, or consciousness "exist" or "do not exist." One who practices in this way does not claim, "I am practicing the Perfection of Wisdom," nor do they claim, "I am not practicing it." They do not claim, "I am both practicing and not practicing," nor do they claim, "I am neither practicing nor not practicing." Shariputra, a bodhisattva mahasattva who practices in this way is said to strive in the Perfection of Wisdom. Shariputra, furthermore, a bodhisattva mahasattva practicing the Perfection of Wisdom does not practice the Perfection of Wisdom for the sake of the Perfection of Generosity. They do not practice the Perfection of Wisdom for the sake of the Perfection of Ethics, the Perfection of Patience, the Perfection of Effort, the Perfection of Concentration, or the Perfection of Wisdom itself. They do not practice the Perfection of Wisdom for the sake of the level of non-retrogression <note>the stage from which a bodhisattva will never fall back from the path</note>. They do not practice for the sake of maturing sentient beings, or for the sake of purifying a Buddha-field, or for the sake of the Tathagata.
<leaf-break/>
The bodhisattva mahasattva is said to strive in the Perfection of Wisdom. They do not practice the Perfection of Wisdom for the sake of the divine eye. They do not practice the Perfection of Wisdom for the sake of the divine ear, knowing the minds of others, recollecting past lives, or the domain of miracles. Why is that? Because one practicing the Perfection of Wisdom in this way does not truly perceive even the Perfection of Wisdom itself, let alone a bodhisattva. How could there be any supernormal knowledge in any manner? Shariputra, a bodhisattva mahasattva who practices the Perfection of Wisdom in this way is said to be striving. Shariputra, furthermore, a bodhisattva mahasattva practicing the Perfection of Wisdom thinks: "By the divine eye, I shall know the deaths and births of sentient beings dwelling in worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the eastern direction. By the divine ear, I shall hear their sounds. I shall also know their minds. Having recollected their past lives, I shall go there through miracles and teach the Dharma."

Everything up to purification is also neither bound nor liberated. Why is that? Because consciousness itself does not exist, consciousness is neither bound nor liberated. Venerable Purna, all phenomena are neither bound nor liberated. Why is that? Because all phenomena do not exist, they are neither bound nor liberated. Likewise, because of being empty and so forth, they are neither bound nor liberated. Venerable Purna, the perfection of generosity is neither bound nor liberated. Likewise, the perfection of discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of diligence, the perfection of meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom are neither bound nor liberated. Because they do not exist, they are neither bound nor liberated. Because of being empty and so forth, they are neither bound nor liberated. Venerable Purna, inner emptiness is also neither bound nor liberated. Venerable Purna, everything up to the emptiness of the nature of non-entities is also neither bound nor liberated. Venerable Purna, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment are also neither bound nor liberated. Venerable Purna, everything up to the ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four kinds of analytical knowledge, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha is also neither bound...

<leaf-break/>

Those who are to be [liberated] are also neither bound nor liberated. The Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who are to be honored, are also neither bound nor liberated. The dharma to be heard is also neither bound nor liberated. Never being separated from the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, is also neither bound nor liberated. Not being separated from the superknowledges <note>original: "abhijñā"</note>, not being separated from the five eyes, and not being separated from the meditative concentrations <note>original: "samādhi"</note> is also neither bound nor liberated. Giving rise to the knowledge of the paths is also neither bound nor liberated. Realizing omniscience is also neither bound nor liberated. Turning the wheel of dharma is also neither bound nor liberated. Liberating sentient beings through the three vehicles is also neither bound nor liberated. Venerable Purna, because they are non-existent, empty, and unproduced, the Bodhisattva Mahasattva is also neither bound nor liberated; they will realize all phenomena through the six perfections. This concludes the fourteenth chapter of the Perfection of Wisdom in Eighteen Thousand Lines, titled "Neither Bound Nor Liberated."

...one should contemplate in the manner of non-perception. Kaushika, furthermore, a bodhisattva mahasattva, having generated the mind endowed with omniscience, meditates on the four foundations of mindfulness, and meditates in the manner of non-perception. Likewise, they meditate on the four right efforts, the four bases of miraculous power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, the eightfold noble path, the ten powers of a Tathagata, the four fearlessnesses, the four specific authentic cognitions, and the eighteen unmixed qualities of a Buddha; they meditate on these in the manner of non-perception. Kaushika, furthermore, a bodhisattva mahasattva, having generated the mind endowed with omniscience, practices the perfection of generosity, and practices it in the manner of non-perception. Likewise, having generated the mind endowed with omniscience, they practice the perfection of ethics, the perfection of patience, the perfection of diligence, the perfection of concentration, and the perfection of wisdom; they practice these in the manner of non-perception. Kaushika, furthermore, when a bodhisattva mahasattva [practices] the perfection of wisdom...

<leaf-break/>

...is the perfection of wisdom of the bodhisattva mahasattva. When that was said, Shakra, the lord of the gods, said to the long-lived Subhuti: Venerable Subhuti, how is it that the mind of dedication is not accompanied by the mind of awakening? How is it that the mind of awakening is not accompanied by the mind of dedication? How is it that the mind of dedication does not exist and is not perceived in the mind of awakening? How is it that the mind of awakening does not exist and is not perceived in the mind of dedication? Subhuti replied: Kaushika, whatever is the mind of dedication is not "mind," and whatever is the mind of awakening is also not "mind." That which is "not mind" in that way is inconceivable. Since that which is inconceivable is also not an act of thinking, the "non-mind" does not perform a dedication as a "non-mind," and the inconceivable does not perform a dedication as the inconceivable. In that way, whatever is "not mind" is the inconceivable, and what is inconceivable is also "not mind." Kaushika, that is the perfection of wisdom of the bodhisattva mahasattva. Then the Bhagavan <note>the Blessed One</note> spoke these verses: For example, as many as the grains of sand in the Ganges, I remember infinite eons ago, when the Protector of the World named Melody of Eloquence appeared. Within his teachings, there was a wise monk who held the Dharma. The King's son heard this meditative concentration as it was explained by him. He offered his own garments and made a full dedication of merit; then, having been seen by that Protector Buddha, he attained the enlightenment of Immeasurable Life <note>Amitayus</note>. Whatever karmic actions were previously done, their results were entirely exhausted by hearing this mass of primordial wisdom. Furthermore, when the Buddha Stainless Moon explained this meditative concentration, a merchant's son heard it, abandoned his household, and went forth. Without sleep or regret, and without even putting on sandals, he practiced this meditative concentration for ten thousand years. At the very moment of hearing this, he attained supreme enlightenment, and never again desired a home, wealth, or took pleasure in enjoyments. Having seen the infinite Buddhas, all...

<leaf-break/>

...the arrogant one, who feels pride toward others, thinks "I have reached the end of enlightenment." By finding relics, seeing light, or making offerings to the Victor, his hair stands on end. Because he thinks he has attained enlightenment, he feels a slight sense of wonder. Because enlightenment is very far away, through these deceits of his, he is diminished, and once again the Victor is very far from him. Even after hearing these discourses, thinking "I know I will attain enlightenment" and thinking "I will quickly see Immeasurable Life; I will quickly see the Buddha," if he dwells on mental objects, enlightenment is very far away. For those who do not strive for the true limit of reality, no prophecy is given. After seeing this merchant's son give away his treasury of wealth and later go forth, they remain attached to houses that give alms. This kind of meditative concentration, I heard it in the past from the Buddha Dipamkara <note>gloss: "The Igniter of Lamps"</note>. For those who do not know the truth, nothing will arise. Because they want a priceless jewel, like carrying a load of grass to the ocean, those fools go forth and rely on the height of intellectual profit. In this, one is not purified by learning, ethics, or going forth. In this accomplishment of the path to enlightenment, dwell with conscientiousness. Whoever in the future time explains...

is seven leagues of radiance. Gaits of the Deer is the father. Beautiful Form is the mother. Naga is the son. Wanderer of the Continents is the attendant. Majesty of Beings is the scholar. སུམ་ཁྲི་དྲུག་སྟོང་གནས། །མཆོད་རྟེན་དཔག་ཚད་བརྒྱད་པ་འབྱུང་འགྱུར་ཏེ། །རིན་ཆེན་བརྒྱ་ཡི་དྲ་བས་རྣམ་པར་སྤྲས། །མི་ཡི་འདྲེན་པ་དབྱངས་དག་སྙན་པ་ཡི། །སྐྱེ་

གསེར་ལས་བྱས་པའི་བླ་རེ་ཕུལ་ནས་ཀྱང་། །དང་པོར་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཏུ་ནི་སེམས་བསྐྱེད་དོ།། །བདེ་གཤེགས་མི་བསྙེངས་རོལ་མོ་མཁན་གྱུར་ཚེ། །དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པམི་འཇིགས་སྦྱིན་དེ་ལ།།
<leaf-break/>
སྟོན་པ་བླ་མ་ལ། །ཤ་ཁ་ར་ཡི་རི་ལུ་ཕུལ་ནས་ཀྱང་། །དང་པོར་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཏུ་ནི་སེམས་བསྐྱེད་དོ། །བདེ་གཤེགས་འོད་དཔག་མེད་པ་བླ་མའི་ཚེ། །དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པ་བཀོད་པའི་འོད་དེ་ལ། །གདུགས་
གཅིག་ཅིག་ནི་དབུལ་བ་བྱས་ནས་ཀྱང་། །དང་པོར་བྱུང་ཆུབ་ཏུ་ནི་སེམས་བསྐྱེད་དེ། །དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པ་ཀླུ་སྦྱིན་འཕྲེང་རྒྱུད་ཚེ། །དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་བ་སེང་གེ་རྣམ་བསྒྱིངས་ལ། །མེ་ཏོག་དག་གི་
ཆུན་པོ་ཕུལ་ནས་ཀྱང་། །དང་བོར་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཏུ་ནི་སེམས་སྐྱེད་དོ། །བདེ་གཤེགས་བརྟན་གཤེགས་ནོར་བུ་མཁན་གྱུར་ཚེ། །དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་ཡིད་གཉིས་སྤོང་དེ་ལ། །རིན་པོ་ཆེ་ཡི་དྲ་བ་
ཕུལ་ནས་ཀྱང་། །དང་པོ་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཏུ་ནི་སེམས་བསྐྱེས་དོ། །བདེ་གཤེགས་དོན་ཡོད་མཐོང་བ་ནད་པའི་གསོས་སྨན་ལ། །སྦྱོར་མཁས་བུར་གྱུར་ཚེ་ན་དགེ་སློང་དགེ་འདུན་དག །སྤྱན་དྲངས་ནད་
སྨན་སྦྱར་ནས་བདེ་གཤེགས་ལེགས་མཐོང་ལ། །དང་པོར་ཁོ་ནར་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཏུ་ནི་སེམས་བསྐྱོད་དོ། །བདེ་གཤེགས་བརྩོན་འགྲུས་སྦྱིན་པ་འཁོར་ལོས་སྒྱུར་རྒྱལ་ཚེ། །ཙན་དན་དམར་པོ་དག་ལས་
གཙུག་ལག་ཁང་བརྒྱ་སྟོང་། །བྱས་ཏེ་རས་བཅོས་གཡོགས་ནས་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པ་པོ། །བདུད་རྩིའི་སྟབས་ལ་དང་པོར་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཏུ་ནི་སེམས་བསྐྱེད་དོ། །བདེ་གཤེགས་བཟང་སྐྱོང་གིས་ནི་བདེ་
གཤེགས་ཟླ་བའི་འོད། །ཉན་ཐོས་བཅས་པའི་དགེ་འདུན་འཁོར་བཅས་ཁྲི་ཕྲག་ཅུ། །ཞག་བདུན་བར་དུ་ཞལ་ཟས་རོ་ནི་བརྒྱ་ལྡན་པས། །ཚིམ་པར་མཛད་དེ་དང་པོར་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་བསྐྱེད་དོ། །བདེ

at that time, he offered a measure of flour and first generated the mind for enlightenment.
When the Sugata Firm Speech was the son of a shell merchant and scattered a handful of shells as an offering to the Sugata Unmoved, he first generated the mind for enlightenment.
When the Sugata Without Pride was a prince desiring joy and made offerings of songs and melodies to the Tathagata Infinite Arrangement, he first generated the mind for enlightenment.
When the Sugata Light Maker was a universal monarch and offered precious robes to the Tathagata Heap of Radiant Brilliance, he first generated the mind for enlightenment.
When the Tathagata Great Meru offered seven Ashoka flowers to the Tathagata Abiding Intelligence, he first generated the mind for enlightenment.
When the Sugata Vajra God was Indra, king of gods, and caused a rain of <term>mandarava</term> <gloss>coral tree</gloss> flowers to fall upon the Tathagata Steadfast, he first generated the mind for enlightenment.
When the Tathagata Possessing Discipline was a king of Jambudvipa <gloss>the southern continent</gloss> and offered a canopy made of gold to the Sugata Joy of Liberation, he first generated the mind for enlightenment.
When the Sugata Without Fear was a musician and offered... to the Tathagata Giver of Fearlessness...

<leaf-break/>

offered a pellet of sugar to the Teacher, the Guru, and first generated the mind for enlightenment.
When the Sugata Infinite Light was a guru and offered a single parasol to the Tathagata Radiant Arrangement, he first generated the mind for enlightenment.
When the Tathagata Giver of Nagas was a garland weaver and offered a bouquet of flowers to the Tathagata Lion's Stretch, he first generated the mind for enlightenment.
When the Sugata Steadfast Arrival was a jeweler and offered a net of precious gems to the Tathagata Abandoner of Hesitation, he first generated the mind for enlightenment.
When the Sugata Meaningful Vision was an expert in compounding medicinal cures for the sick and invited the assembly of monks, preparing medicines for them, he first generated the mind for enlightenment before the Sugata Fine Vision.
When the Sugata Giver of Diligence was a universal monarch and built a hundred thousand monasteries out of red sandalwood, covered them with fine cotton, and offered them to the Tathagata Ambrosial Step, he first generated the mind for enlightenment.
When the Sugata Protector of Goodness satisfied the Sugata Moon Radiance and his retinue of ten thousand disciples for seven days with food of a hundred flavors, he first generated the mind for enlightenment.

ཡང་ཆགས་པ་མེད་དོ། །ནང་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱང་ཆགས་པ་མེད་དོ། །ཕྱི་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱང་ཆགས་པར་མེད་དོ། །ཕྱི་ནང་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱང་ཆག་པ་མེད་དོ། །སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱང་ཆགས་པས་མེད་
དོ། །ཆེན་པོ་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱང་ཆགས་མེད་དོ། །དོན་དམ་པ་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱང་ཆགས་པའི་མེད་དོ། །འདུས་བྱས་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱང་ཆགས་པ། མེད་དོ། །འདུས་མ་བྱས་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱང་ཆག་པར་མེད་
དོ། །མཐའ་ལས་འདས་པ་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱང་ཆག་པ་མད་དོ། །ཐོག་མ་དང་ཐ་མ་མེད་པ་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱང་ཆགསཔ་མེད་དོ། །དོར་བ་མེད་པ་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱང་ལགས་པ་མེད་དོ། །རང་
བཞིན་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱང་ཆགས་བ་མེད་དོ། །ཆོས་ཐམས་ཅད་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱང་ཆགས་ལ་མེད་དོ། །རང་གི་མཚན་ཉིད་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱང་ལགས་བ་མེད་དོ། །མི་དམིགས་པ་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱང་
ཆགས་པ་མེད་དོ། །དངོས་པོ་མེད་པ་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱང་མ་ཆགས་པ་མེད་དོ། །ངོ་བོ་ཉིད་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱང་མ་ཆག་པ་མེད་དོ། །དངོས་པོ་མད་པའི་ངོ་བོ་ཉིད་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱང། མ་ཆགས་པ་མེད་དོ། །

there is no <note>attachment</note>. The perfection of diligence is also without attachment. The perfection of meditative concentration is also without attachment. The perfection of wisdom is also without attachment. Inner emptiness is also without attachment. Outer emptiness is also without attachment. Outer and inner emptiness is also without attachment. The emptiness of emptiness is also without attachment. Great emptiness is also without attachment. Ultimate emptiness is also without attachment. Conditioned emptiness is also without attachment. Unconditioned emptiness is also without attachment. Emptiness that transcends limits is also without attachment. Emptiness without beginning or end is also without attachment. Emptiness of non-discarding is also without attachment. Emptiness of nature is also without attachment. Emptiness of all phenomena is also without attachment. Emptiness of self-characteristics is also without attachment. Unobservable emptiness is also without attachment. Emptiness of non-existence is also without attachment. Emptiness of essence is also without attachment. The emptiness of the essence of non-existence is also without attachment. The applications of mindfulness are also without attachment. The right efforts are also without attachment. The bases of miraculous power are also without attachment. The faculties are also without attachment.

<leaf-break/>

Subhuti, regarding what you said: "The mind of omniscience <note>original: "thams cad mkhyen pa nyid kyi sems"</note> itself is also without stains and without containment," it is just so. Venerable Subhuti, it is not only that; even the minds of ordinary beings are without stains and without containment because their nature is emptiness. The minds of Hearers <term>Sravakas</term> and Solitary Realizers <term>Pratyekabuddhas</term>, and the minds of the Blessed Buddhas are also without stains and without containment because their nature is emptiness. Subhuti said: "It is so. Venerable Saradvatiputra, the minds of ordinary beings are without stains and without containment because their nature is emptiness. The minds of Hearers are without stains and without containment because their nature is emptiness. The minds of Solitary Realizers are also without stains and without containment because their nature is emptiness. The minds of the Blessed Buddhas are also without stains and without containment because their nature is emptiness." [Saradvatiputra] said: "Venerable Subhuti, if that is so, then form is also without stains and without containment because its nature is emptiness. Feeling is also without stains and without containment because its nature is emptiness. Perception is also its nature is emptiness."

until he reaches enlightenment, he will never be separated from the mindfulness of the Buddha. This is the Bodhisattva Mahasattva's purification of devotion to the Buddha’s body. In that regard, what is the Bodhisattva Mahasattva's purification of the discernment of phenomena? Whether the Tathagata is present or has passed into final nirvana, he teaches the Dharma to sentient beings: virtuous in the beginning, virtuous in the middle, and virtuous in the end; with excellent words and excellent meaning; unadulterated, complete, pure, and purified in the holy life. This consists of the correct teaching of the twelve branches of scripture: the discourses <note>sūtra</note>, songs <note>geya</note>, prophecies <note>vyākaraṇa</note>, verses <note>gāthā</note>, aphorisms <note>udāna</note>, introductory narratives <note>nidāna</note>, legends <note>avadāna</note>, past lives <note>itivṛttaka</note>, birth stories <note>jātaka</note>, extensive teachings <note>vaipulya</note>, marvelous accounts <note>adbhutadharma</note>, and established instructions <note>upadeśa</note>. This is the Bodhisattva Mahasattva's purification of the discernment of phenomena. In that regard, what is the Bodhisattva Mahasattva's purification of removing pride and arrogance? By removing pride and arrogance in this way, he will never be born into a low family. This is—

<leaf-break/>

the purification. In that regard, what is the Bodhisattva Mahasattva's abiding in the power of patience? It is a mind that is without malice and without harm toward all sentient beings. This is the Bodhisattva Mahasattva's abiding in the power of patience. In that regard, what is the Bodhisattva Mahasattva's experiencing of great joy and enthusiasm? It is this: bringing all sentient beings to maturity in the three vehicles. This is the Bodhisattva Mahasattva's experiencing of great joy and enthusiasm. In that regard, what is the Bodhisattva Mahasattva's not abandoning all sentient beings? It is the protecting of all sentient beings in this way. This is the Bodhisattva Mahasattva's not abandoning all sentient beings. In that regard, what is the Bodhisattva Mahasattva's manifestation of great compassion? A Bodhisattva Mahasattva, when practicing the conduct of a Bodhisattva, thinks: "For the sake of even a single sentient being, I shall remain in the hells for as many eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges river, until all sentient beings are established in the wisdom of a Buddha, even if I am cut and hacked in those places."

ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོ་འདིས་ཀྱང་ལྷ་དང་། མི་དང་། ལྷ་མ་ཡིན་དུ་བཅས་པའི་འཇིག་རྟེན་ཟིལ་གྱིས་མནན་ཞིང་འབྱུང་བར་མི་འགྱུར་ཏེ། རབ་འབྱོར་བཟོད་པའི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་བྱིན་པ་དངོས་པོ་མེད་ལ་དངོས་
པོ་མ་ཡིན་པས། དེའི་ཕྱིར་ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོ་འདིས་ལྷ་དང་། མི་དང་། ལྷ་ཡིན་དུ་བཅས་པའི་འཇིག་རྟན་ཟིལ་གྱིས་མནན་ཅིང་འབྱང་བ་ཡིན་ནོ། །རབ་འབྱོརགལ་ཏེ་བརྩོན་འགྲུས་ཀྱི་
ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་དངོས་པ་ཡོད་པ་ཞིག་ཡིན་ཏེ། དངོད་པོ་མེད་པ་མ་ཡིན་ན་ན། ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོ་འདིས་ཀྱང་། ལྷ་དང་། མི་དང་། ལྷ་མོ་ཡིན་དུ་བཅས་པའི་འཇིགས་རྟེན་ཟིལ་གྱིས་མནན་ཅིང་། འབྱུང་
བར་མི་འགྱུར་ཏེ། རབ་འབྱར་བརྩོན་འགྲུས་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་དངོས་བོ་མེད་ལ་དངོས་པོ་མ་ཡིན་པས། དེའི་ཕྱིར། ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོ་འདིས་ལྷ་དག། མི་དང་། ལྷ་མ་ཡིན་ཏུ་བཅས་པའི་འཇིག་རྟེན
ཟིལ་གྱིས་མནན་ཅིང་འབྱུང་བ་ཡིན་ནོ། །རབ་འབྱར་གལ་ཏེ་བསམ་གཏན་གྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་དངོས་པོ་ཡོད་པ་ཞིག་ཡིན་ཏེ། དགོས་པོ་མེད་པ་མ་ཡིན་ན་ནི། ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོ་འདིས་ཡང་
ལྷ་དང་། མི་དང་། ལྷ་མ་ཡིན་དུ་བཅས་པའི་འཇིག་རྟེན་ཟིལ་གྱིས་མནན་ཞིང་འབྱུང་བར་མི་འགྱུར་ཏེ། རབ་འབྱོར་བསམ་གཏན་གྱི་ཕ་རོལ་དུ་ཕྱིན་པ་དངོས་པོ་མེད་ལ། དངོས་པོ་མ་ཡིན་པས།

༄༅། །འདིས་ལྷ་དང་། མི་དང་། ལྷ་མ་ཡིན་དུ་བཅས་པའི་འཇིག་རྟེན་ཟིལ་གྱིས་མནན་ཅིང་འབྱུང་བ་ཡིན་ནོ། །རབ་འབྱོར་གལ་ཏེ་ཕྱི་ནང་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་དངོས་པོ་ཡོད་པ་ཞིག་ཡིན་
ཏེ། དངོས་པོ་མེད་པ་མ་ཡིན་ན་ནི། ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོ་འདིས་ཀྱང་ལྷ་དང་། མི་དང་། ལྷ་ མ་ཡིན་དུ་བཅས་པའི་འཇིགས་རྟེན་ཟིལ་གྱིས་མནན་ཅིང་བྱུང་བར་མི་འགྱུར་ཏེ། རབ་འབྱོར་ཕྱི་ནང་སྟོང་པ་
ཉིད་དངོས་པོ་མེད་ལ་དངོས་པོ་མ་ཡིན་པས། དེའི་ཕྱིར་ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོ་འདིས་ལྷ་དང་། མི་དང་ལྷ་མ་ཡིན་དུ་བཅས་པའི་འཛིག་རྟེན་ཟིལ་གྱིས་མནན་ཅིག་འབྱུང་བ་ཡིན་ནོ། །རབ་ འབྱོར་གལ་ཏེ་
སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་དངོས་པོ་ཡོང་པ་ཞིག་ཡིན་ཏེ། དངོས་པོ་མེད་པ་མ་ ཡིན་ན་ནི། ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་ པོ་འདིས་ཀྱང་ལྷ་དང་། མ་དང་། ལྷ་མ་ཡིན་དུ་ བཅས་པའི་འཇིག་རྟེན་ཟིལ་ཀྱིས་མནན་
ཅིང་འབྱུང་བར་མི་འགྱུར་ཏེ། རབའབྱོར་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ དངོས་པོ་མེད་ལ་དངོས་པོམ་ཡིན་པས། དེའི་ཕྱིར་ ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོ་འདིས་ལྷ་ དང་། མི་དང་། ལྷ་མ་ཡིན་དུ་བཅས་པའི་ འཇིག་རྟེན་ཟིལ་གྱིས་
མནན་ཅིང་འབྱུང་བ་ཡིན་ནོ། །རབའབྱོར་གལ་ཏེ་ཆེན་པོ་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་དངོས་པོ་ ཡོད་པ་ཞིག་ཡིན་ཏེ། དངོས་ པོ་མེད་པ་མ་ཡིན་ན་ནི། ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོ་འདིས་ཀྱང་ལྷ་དང་། མི་དང་། ལྷ་མ་ ཡིན་དུ་
བཅས་པའི་འཇིག་རྟེན་ཟིལ་གྱིས་མནན་ ཅིང་འབྱུང་བར་མི་འགྱུར་ ཏེ། རབ་འབྱོར་ཆེན་པོ་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་དངོསཔོ་མེད་ལ་ དངོས་པོ་མ་ཡིན་པས། དེའི་ཕྱིར་ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོ་འདིས་ལྷ་དང་། མི་དང་།

དང་། དེ་བཞིན་ཉིད་གང་ཡིན་པ་དང་། ཡང་དག་པའི་མཐའ་གང་ཡིན་པ་དང་། བསམ་གྱིས་མི་ཁྱབ་པའི་དབྱིངས་གང་ཡིན་པ་དང་། མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པའི་
དབྱིངས་གང་ཡིན་པའི་ཆོས་དེ་དག་ཐམས་ཅད་ནི་ལྡན་པ་ཡང་མ་ཡིན། མི་ལྡན་པ་ཡང་མ་ཡིན་ཏེ། གཟུགས་མེད་པ། བསྟན་དུ་མེད་པ། ཐོགས་པ་མེད་པ་འདི་ལྟར་མཚན་ཉིད་
མེད་པར་མཚན་ཉིད་གཅིག་པ་ཤ་སྟག་སྟེ། རབ་འབྱོར་རྣམ་གྲངས་འདིས་ན། ཁྱོད་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་དང་མཐུན་པར་ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོ་སྟོན་ཏོ། །དེ་ཅིའི་
ཕྱིར་ཞེ་ན། ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོ་ཡང་གཞན་ལ། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིནཔ་ཡང་གཞན་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་མེད་དེ། དེ་ལྟར་ན་ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོ་དང་། ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་དུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ཡང་
གཉིས་སུ་མེད་དེ་གཉིས་སུ་བྱར་མེད་དོ། །ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོ་ཡང་གཞན་པ། བསམ་གཏན་གྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ཡང་གཞན་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་མེ་དེ་དེ། དེ་ལྟར་ན་ཐེག་པ་ཆེ་པོ་དང་། བསམ་
གཏན་གྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ། ཡང་གཉིས་སུ་མེད་དེ་གཉིས་སུ་བར་མེད་དོ། །ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པ་ཡང་གཞན་ལ། བརྩོན་འགྲུས་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ཡང་བཞན་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་མེད་དེ། །དེ་ལྟར་ན་ཐེག་པ་

"Blessed One, through how many countless eons are these unfavorable states completely abandoned?" "Avalokiteśvara, through three: by immeasurable eons composed of seasons, months, half-months, days, days and nights, sessions, half-sessions, moments, instants, and brief flashes." "Blessed One, what is the character of the arising of afflictions for Bodhisattvas on these stages? What are the faults? What should be understood as the qualities?" "Avalokiteśvara, the character is one of being without total affliction. Why is that? Because on the first Bodhisattva stage, one initially realizes the entire sphere of reality <term>dharmadhātu</term>. Therefore, the afflictions of a Bodhisattva arise with awareness and not without awareness. Thus, the character is the absence of total affliction. "The causes of existence and the afflictions will be completely pacified. Even for eons as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, they will turn away from them. The karmic obscurations and causes of existence of women who have committed the immediate <note>uninterrupted</note> sins will be exhausted, even to the point where nothing remains. They will reach the point of exhausting all defilements and possessing the bliss of complete liberation." Then, at that time, the Bodhisattva Mahasattva Akashagarbha <note>Essence of Space</note> approached the Blessed One, bowed with palms pressed together, and addressed him with these verses:
"You are the sole captain. You are certain about all phenomena. Respect has been born from seeing you. You also uphold the glory of a spiritual friend. By offering a single flower and incense to the Tathagata, you uphold the beloved spiritual friend who possesses the excellence of all limbs. Although a great assembly has gathered here at one time, all the gods recite mantras and uphold the vast glory of the spiritual friend. The Protector of the World has shown this only once. The non-gods always possess wisdom. The spiritual friend..."

<leaf-break/>

"...are your followers free from weariness? Are you free from little harms? Are those who wish to hear the holy Dharma present? Do they apply themselves to the essence of that Dharma just as they have heard it from the Lord of Dharma? Do they dwell by means of the dwelling of the Dharma? Have you conquered the realm of Mara and the realm of the Nagas in this Buddha-field? Is this solely your Buddha-realm? Have you turned the wheel of the Dharma here without obstruction? For the sake of whoever will turn the wheel in this Buddha-field, the Tathagata Flower Essence of Glory gives faith to you and to this chapter of rays that destroys the realm of the Nagas, the Dharma of the Sun's Essence, and this dharani that arises from the karma of sentient beings." Then, the pacifying dharani from within the womb of peaceful vidya, which has great power, great benefits, benefits all sentient beings, pacifies all diseases, subdues all afflictions, causes full understanding of all aggregates and sense-fields, distinguishes all phenomena, and correctly demonstrates all methods...

The Elder Ajnata Kaundinya said to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, please bless the <term>nagas</term>. Please cause this Dharma discourse, which is connected to the conduct of showing inconceivable karma, to blaze for a long time." The Blessed One declared: "As long as these great <term>stupas</term> <gloss>reliquary monuments</gloss> in this four-continent world are not emptied of all those who are diligent in mental yoga, so long will this Dharma discourse be practiced in this four-continent world. Which are the great <term>stupas</term>? Here in Jambudvipa, this dwelling place of the Sage that supports all is where many past Buddhas, <term>bodhisattvas</term>, <term>pratyekabuddhas</term> <gloss>solitary realizers</gloss>, and <term>shravakas</term> resided, and where they will reside in the future. To cause the great teaching to remain for a long time, the past perfectly enlightened Buddhas entrusted this dwelling place of the Sage to the hands of Varuna <gloss>God of Water</gloss>. I also entrust it into his hands so that it may be spread—"

<leaf-break/>

"—and by the command of the Blessed One, I shall protect everything from the dwelling place of the Sage, including those who live by the Dharma and are diligent in equanimity, and those donors and patrons who are diligent in honoring and serving those who live by the Dharma and are diligent in equanimity, as long as those disciples reside without being seized." The Blessed One declared: "Lord of <term>nagas</term>, excellent, excellent! By being blessed in this way, such great patrons will cause my way of Dharma to blaze for a long time. On the side of the continent of Aparagodaniya, on that mountain of dust, the colorful dwelling place of the Sage is entrusted to the <term>naga</term> king Rinchen Trengwa-chen <note>Possessing a Jewel Garland</note> to hold," and so on. The <term>naga</term> king Rinchen Trengwa-chen said: "Venerable Blessed One, it is so. The Tathagata Vishvabhu entrusted that colorful dwelling place of the Sage there to be held," and so on.
